content:
Let one ox eat 1 unit/day.  
If \(x\) oxen eat as much as 3 buffaloes or 4 cows, then:
\[
\text{buffalo}=\frac{x}{3},\quad \text{cow}=\frac{x}{4}
\]

Initially:
\[
15\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)+8+24\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)
=5x+8+6x=11x+8
\]
Fodder lasts 36 days, so total fodder:
\[
36(11x+8)
\]

After adding 15 buffaloes and 40 cows:
\[
30\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)+8+64\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)
=10x+8+16x=26x+8
\]
This lasts 18 days, so:
\[
36(11x+8)=18(26x+8)
\]
\[
22x+16=26x+8
\]
\[
x=2
\]

Therefore, \(\boxed{2}\) oxen eat as much as 3 buffaloes or 4 cows.
